paper_a.title: Dirac's theorem on chordal graphs implies Brooks' theorem

paper_b.title: Yet another proof of Brooks' theorem

metadata.description: Both papers prove Brooks' theorem on graph coloring but by fundamentally different routes. Paper A (Feghali) derives Brooks from Dirac's theorem on chordal graphs, going through a list-coloring lemma on chordal graphs and then a list-color generalization of Brooks; the chordless cycle of a minimum counterexample is exploited to build two reduced graphs F, H. Paper B (Rabern) gives a direct minimum-counterexample proof that extracts an induced K_Delta or odd cycle from G - M (M maximal independent), then glues two non-adjacent vertices in the neighborhood to obtain a smaller K_{Delta+1}-free graph. The shared statement (Brooks' theorem) and the shared minimum-counterexample / glue-and-extend skeleton make this a textbook alternative-proof pair.

matches.explanation: Both nodes state Brooks' Theorem. Paper A states it in the standard 'connected G != K_{Delta+1} with maximum degree Delta has a Delta-coloring' form (Delta >= 3); Paper B states the contrapositive 'chi(G) = Delta(G)+1 >= 4 implies G contains K_{Delta(G)+1}'. These are the same theorem up to equivalent formulation. Paper A tags it origin=external (cites Brooks 1941); Paper B tags origin=paper but also cites Brooks 1941 — the underlying mathematical content is identical.

Paper A's main contribution is the list-color Brooks' Theorem (Vizing; Erdos-Rubin-Taylor): under list assignment with |L(v)| >= Delta, G has an L-coloring. Paper B does not state or prove this list-coloring strengthening; its scope is the classical (non-list) Brooks' theorem only.

Paper A's Lemma 1 (list-coloring of chordal graphs by clique number) is the bridge through which Dirac's theorem on chordal graphs is invoked. Paper B uses no chordal-graph machinery at all, so this lemma has no counterpart.
Proof of Lemma 1 (greedy along the perfect elimination ordering). Tied to paper A's chordal/PEO machinery, which paper B does not use.

Both are minimum-counterexample proofs of Brooks' theorem (parent-level proof match). They share the high-level skeleton: take a minimum counterexample G, identify a structured subgraph (a chordless cycle of length >= 4 in A; an induced K_Delta or odd cycle T in G - M in B), modify G to a smaller K_{Delta+1}-free graph that can be colored by minimality (F or H in A; H = (G - T) +/- xy in B), then extend the partial coloring around the structured subgraph to a contradiction. The technical hearts differ: A leans on a list-color Brooks (which it proves) and uses chordless-cycle modifications, while B uses a maximal independent set M to reduce Delta and then performs a vertex-gluing. Hence parent proofs are analogous, not exact.

Composite Level-2 step alignment under the parent proof match (PP431.2 ~ PP413.1). The two step DAGs share a common shape but differ in the technical objects: 'take minimum counterexample' (PSP431.3 ~ PSP413.1, with B additionally deriving Delta-regularity); 'identify problematic substructure' (PSP431.4 + PSP431.5 use the chordal-graph lemma to force a chordless cycle C, vs PSP413.2 uses a maximal independent set to extract an induced K_Delta or odd cycle T); 'reduce to a smaller K_{Delta+1}-free graph by local edge surgery' (PSP431.5 + PSP431.6 build F, H by removing cycle vertices and adding chord edges and pick the K_{Delta+1}-free side, vs PSP413.3 + PSP413.4 rule out K_{Delta+1} - e and then glue two non-adjacent vertices x, y in N(T)); 'color the smaller graph by minimality and extend to a contradiction' (PSP431.7 + PSP431.8 + PSP431.9 + PSP431.10 vs PSP413.5). Step granularities differ (8 vs 5) and the precise combinatorial moves differ, so the composite is analogous rather than exact.

Dirac's theorem on chordal graphs (chordal iff admits a perfect elimination ordering) is the central external tool of paper A's approach. Paper B uses no chordal-graph theory and so has nothing matching this cited theorem.
Definition of 'chordal graph' is paper-original to A and unused in B.
Definition of 'perfect elimination ordering' is paper-original to A and unused in B.
Definition of 'list assignment' is needed only for paper A's list-coloring statements; paper B does not consider list coloring.
Definition of 'L-colorable' is part of paper A's list-coloring vocabulary, with no counterpart in paper B.

Paper A defines 'proper k-coloring' explicitly as an assignment phi : V -> {1,...,k} with phi(u) != phi(v) for adjacent u,v. Paper B does not define proper coloring as a standalone node, but its DP413.1 introduces the chromatic number chi(G) as 'the minimum number of colors needed to properly color the vertices of G so that adjacent vertices receive distinct colors', which encapsulates the same notion. The match is at the 'proper coloring concept' level; types are both 'definition'.
